export const meta = {
  name: 'bonus-pagination',
  description: 'Bonus: server-side leases pagination synced with the URL (service + tests in parallel, then UI)',
  phases: [{ title: 'Build' }, { title: 'UI' }],
}
const COMMON = `Timed build lane (hard deadline 04:05Z for this item). Working dir ./app. ../SPEC.md, ../DECISIONS.md. One simple command per Bash call; never npm i; never commit; NEVER db reset; DB/test commands via bash ../scripts/with-db.sh <cmd>. Dev server at :3000 (never start/kill). Edit ONLY your listed files. Keep it small; existing 1180 tests must stay green.
CONTRACT (exact): src/server/services/leases.ts gains
  export type LeasePage = { items: LeaseListItem[]; total: number; page: number; pageSize: number; pageCount: number; q: string }
  export async function listLeasesPage(ctx: ServiceCtx, params: { q?: string | null; page?: string | number | null; pageSize?: string | number | null }): Promise<LeasePage>
Rules: same visibility and fields as the existing listLeases (staff/manager: own org; tenant: own leases; others 403) and the same ?q= filter (case-insensitive on unit name or tenant name, trimmed; empty = no filter); ordering stable: unit name asc, start_date asc, id asc; pageSize: integer 1..50, default 10, anything invalid -> 10; page: integer >= 1, default 1, anything invalid (non-numeric, 0, negative, decimal) -> 1; a page beyond the last page -> the last page (or 1 when total = 0); total = count with the same where; pageCount = max(1, ceil(total / pageSize)); Prisma skip/take with the SAME where (scoped by the checked org_id / tenant ids). listLeases stays unchanged (GET /api/leases keeps returning the plain array).`
const S = { type: 'object', properties: { status: { type: 'string' }, files_changed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, checks_run: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, assumptions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } }, required: ['status', 'files_changed', 'checks_run', 'assumptions'] }
phase('Build')
const be = agent(`${COMMON}\nTask (backend-engineer): implement listLeasesPage exactly per the CONTRACT in src/server/services/leases.ts (only that file). Reuse the existing listLeases where-building and mapping (refactor into a shared private helper if needed, without changing listLeases' output). Done means: tsc + eslint clean.`,
  { agentType: 'backend-engineer', label: 'page:backend', phase: 'Build', schema: S })
const tests = agent(`${COMMON}\nTask (test-authz): tests/authz/leases-page.test.ts (describe 'R36 R56 leases pagination'). Use tests/helpers createFixtureOrg twice (orgs A, B) and add enough leases to org A by direct pg insert on distinct units (e.g. 12 leases on 12 new units named 'P-01'..'P-12', non-overlapping is automatic on distinct units) using generateSchedule-free inserts (leases only, no invoices needed) — follow tests/helpers/README.md. Call listLeasesPage({ userId }) directly. Assert: manager A page 1 pageSize 5 -> 5 items, total = count of org A leases (from pg), pageCount = ceil(total/5); pages 1..pageCount together contain every org A lease id exactly once and NO org B lease; q='P-1' filters (P-10, P-11, P-12 + 'P-1' itself) and total matches; invalid page ('abc', '0', '-1', '1.5', '') -> page 1; page 999 -> last page; pageSize '0', '51', 'x' -> 10; staff A same as manager; tenant A sees only own leases; user with no membership/tenant -> ApiError 403. The service is being written in parallel by backend-engineer: wait until src/server/services/leases.ts exports listLeasesPage (check with grep; sleep 30 between checks, up to 30) before running. Done means: bash ../scripts/with-db.sh npx vitest run tests/authz/leases-page.test.ts passes.`,
  { agentType: 'test-authz', label: 'page:tests', phase: 'Build', schema: S })
const b = await be
phase('UI')
const ui = await agent(`${COMMON}\nTask (ui-builder): files src/app/(app)/leases/page.tsx and src/components/staff/** only. Switch /leases to listLeasesPage(ctx, { q, page, pageSize }) read from await searchParams. Render 'Showing X–Y of N' and Prev / Next links (Next <Link>) that keep q and pageSize in the URL (omit default values; disabled/hidden at the ends). The existing ?q= search form must reset page to 1 (do not carry page). Empty state unchanged. No client-side fetching for this. Done means: tsc + eslint clean; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/leases?page=abc' returns 307 unauthenticated (login redirect).`,
  { agentType: 'ui-builder', label: 'page:ui', phase: 'UI', schema: S })
return { backend: b, tests: await tests, ui }

backend.status:
done. I added listLeasesPage to src/server/services/leases.ts and changed only that file. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint . --max-warnings=0`, both run from /home/electronica-care/ezy-prep/exam/app, finished with no output, so both are clean. I ran no tests and no DB probes. The new function has not been run against the database yet, so the test lane needs to cover it.

Signature, matching the contract exactly:
`export type LeasePage = { items: LeaseListItem[]; total: number; page: number; pageSize: number; pageCount: number; q: string }`
`export async function listLeasesPage(ctx: ServiceCtx, params: { q?: string | null; page?: string | number | null; pageSize?: string | number | null }): Promise<LeasePage>`

What it does:
- **Who sees what:** I moved listLeases' visibility rule into a shared private helper, `leaseVisibilityWhere(caller)`. Staff and managers get their own org's leases (org_id from memberships). A tenant gets their own leases (tenants.user_id). Anyone else gets 403 from forbidden(). The row mapping is also shared, through `LIST_INCLUDE` and `toListItem`.
- **listLeases is unchanged:** same query, same order (start_date, then id, then a JS sort by unit name), same plain array. GET /api/leases is not touched.
- **Search (q):** q is trimmed; empty means no filter. Otherwise it keeps leases whose unit name or tenant name contains q, ignoring case. This runs in the database and is combined with the visibility rule using AND.
- **Count and page use the same filter:** total is a `count` with the same `where` as the page query, and the page query uses `skip: (page-1)*pageSize, take: pageSize`.
- **Order:** unit name, then start_date, then id, all ascending, so pages never overlap or skip rows.
- **pageSize:** a whole number from 1 to 50, default 10. Anything else gives 10.
- **page:** a whole number of 1 or more, default 1. Anything else gives 1: non-numeric, 0, negative, decimal, "1e1", an empty string, or null. A page past the end becomes the last page, which is 1 when total is 0.
- **pageCount:** max(1, ceil(total / pageSize)).

No new route handler: the contract keeps GET /api/leases as the plain array, so the leases page is expected to call listLeasesPage directly. No new packages are needed.
checks_run: npx tsc --noEmit (from ./app): finished with no output, clean
npx eslint . --max-warnings=0 (from ./app): finished with no output, clean
assumptions: Sort order can differ from the current page. listLeasesPage sorts unit names in PostgreSQL using the database collation. The existing leases page sorts by JS string comparison (character code order). The two orders can differ for mixed-case or non-ASCII unit names. I kept the database order because skip/take needs the database to do the sorting.

Search results can differ slightly too. The new search uses Prisma `contains` with `mode: 'insensitive'` (PostgreSQL ILIKE, with % and _ escaped by Prisma). The current page lower-cases in JS and checks for a substring. ILIKE and JS toLowerCase can disagree on some non-ASCII case rules.

Parsing of page and pageSize, which SPEC does not fix. A string counts only if, after trimming, it is all digits (/^\d+$/). A number counts only if it is a whole number within the safe integer range. Anything else falls back to the default without an error: decimals, '1e1', '+2', '0x10', blank, NaN, Infinity, or values over the limit. pageSize 51 or more gives 10 rather than 50. page has no upper limit except clamping to the last page.

A page past the end becomes the last page. The count and the page query are two separate statements, not one transaction. If leases are added or deleted between them, the page can come back slightly short. I accepted this for a read-only list.
A caller who is both a member of an org and a tenant sees the union of their org's leases and their own tenant leases. This is the same OR rule listLeases already used.
The returned q is the trimmed value, which the UI can use to rebuild Prev/Next links.

No route handler was added. The contract keeps GET /api/leases returning the plain array, so the leases page (UI lane) is expected to call listLeasesPage directly. If the lead wants an HTTP endpoint for the paged list (for example GET /api/leases?page=), that is a separate small task.

tests.status:
done. I wrote one new test file, tests/authz/leases-page.test.ts, with describe 'R36 R56 leases pagination (listLeasesPage service): scoped skip/take, total, clamping'. It has 12 tests and all 12 pass against backend-engineer's listLeasesPage, which was already in src/server/services/leases.ts when I first checked, so I did not have to wait for it. Run output: `bash ../scripts/with-db.sh npx vitest run tests/authz/leases-page.test.ts` -> 'Test Files 1 passed (1)' and 'Tests 12 passed (12)'. `npx tsc --noEmit` and eslint on the file are both clean. I did not run the full suite this lane, so the claim that the existing 1180 tests are still green is unchecked here; the new file only adds its own fixture rows.

Coverage, role x service (all through ctx, Prisma path):
- Manager A: page 1 with pageSize 5 gives 5 items, total equals the org A count read with pg (13), and pageCount = ceil(13/5). Walking every page gives each org A lease exactly once, in the DB's unit name / start_date / id order (a second, earlier lease on P-03 checks the start_date tiebreak). No org B lease appears, including org B's own unit named 'P-10'. Each item's unitName and tenantName match the lease's own unit and tenant in pg.
- q filter: 'P-1' and '  p-1  ' (case-insensitive, trimmed) return exactly P-10, P-11 and P-12, with total 3. The returned q is the trimmed value. Paging the filtered list with pageSize 2 gives the same rows. Empty, whitespace, null and undefined q all mean no filter. A q with no match gives total 0, page 1, pageCount 1.
- page: 'abc', '0', '-1', '1.5', '', 0, -3, 1.5 and null all give page 1 with the first 5 ids. Page '999' gives the last page with the right final slice.
- pageSize: '0', '51', 'x', '2.5', -1 and a missing value all give 10. '50' is accepted.
- Staff A sees exactly the same pages as manager A.
- Tenant A sees only their own 6 leases (total 6, pageCount 2) and none of tenant B's 7. Manager B sees only org B.
- A user with no membership and no tenant row gets ApiError 403, and so does an unknown user id.

Gaps: there is no HTTP or route test, because GET /api/leases must keep returning the plain array and the page UI belongs to another lane. There is also no test for a user who is both a member and a tenant across two orgs (the OR of both scopes). I found no contract gap: the service matches the brief's contract exactly.
checks_run: bash ../scripts/with-db.sh npx vitest run tests/authz/leases-page.test.ts -> Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 12 passed (12)
assumptions: Expected order is read from pg using `order by u.name asc, l.start_date asc, l.id asc` under the DB's default collation, which is what Prisma's relation orderBy also uses, so the test compares DB order with DB order and not with a JS sort.

Fixture leases are inserted directly with pg as postgres and have no invoices. Pagination only reads leases plus unit and tenant names, and the brief said no invoices were needed. Rows are never deleted (D29); every name is random except the P-xx unit names, which are scoped per fresh org.

Bad numeric inputs (0, -3, 1.5 and -1 as JS numbers) are expected to fall back to the defaults, the same as the bad string forms. The contract says anything invalid falls back, and I read that as covering number inputs too.
Org A is created with units: 0, so its lease count (13) is fixed by the test. Org B gets the fixture lease plus one lease on a unit named 'P-10' to check q does not leak across orgs.

ui.status: Done: /leases now uses listLeasesPage with URL-synced pagination. tsc and eslint are clean, and unauthenticated GET /leases?page=abc returns 307. I did not render the page logged in or run the vitest suite, so the Prev/Next UI is untested in a browser.
checks_run: Not run: authenticated browser render, vitest suite. To see the screen: log in as a seeded manager or staff user and open /leases, /leases?pageSize=2, /leases?pageSize=2&page=2&q=<text>, /leases?page=abc.
assumptions: listLeasesPage and LeasePage already existed in src/server/services/leases.ts with the contracted signature (another lane), so I only changed the page. src/components/staff/** needed no change: LeaseListSkeleton is reused as is.

The page passes raw page and pageSize strings to the service. It uses the service's normalised page and pageSize to build links and the 'Showing X–Y of N' text, so invalid values never reach the URLs it generates.

The page has its own DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = 10, which mirrors the service default and is used only to keep default values out of generated URLs. If the service default changes, this constant must change too.

Prev/Next are Links built as /leases?q=&page=&pageSize=, omitting empty q, page 1 and size 10. At the first or last page they render as non-interactive spans with aria-disabled, not hidden. The label is 'Previous'. The pager shows 'Page N of M' and appears only when total > 0, so the empty state is unchanged.

The search form has no page field, so a new search returns to page 1. It carries pageSize through a hidden input only when the raw value is all digits and not 10; the service still validates it. The Clear link keeps that non-default pageSize.
The Suspense key now includes q, raw page and raw pageSize, so the skeleton shows again on each navigation.
The 'Search unit or tenant' filtering that used to run in the page over the full listLeases array is removed. Filtering and paging now run in the database through the service.

summary: Bonus: server-side leases pagination synced with the URL (service + tests in parallel, then UI)
